# Opener Concepts — Select a Framework, Never Inherit a Formula

Consult this document for openers, product promos, channel intros, and teasers **BEFORE** drafting any scene rundown.

Without an intentional framework, openers for different products converge into the exact same predictable pattern: text zooming in and exiting left $\rightarrow$ 3 icon tiles $\rightarrow$ typing search bar $\rightarrow$ hook $\rightarrow$ feature $\rightarrow$ feature $\rightarrow$ promise $\rightarrow$ logo $\rightarrow$ CTA — even after swapping colors and fonts.
Law #3 enforces novelty of **VISUAL SKIN**; this document enforces novelty of **CONCEPTUAL ARCHITECTURE**.

## Framework Laws

1. **Three Candidates, One Pick**: Prior to finalizing a scene rundown, pitch 3 distinct concept candidates from the menu below (or a bespoke concept), each described in one sentence linking the premise to the target product. Select one based on product traits — choose *what looks most convincing on screen*, not what is easiest to build. Present all three to the user in the style brief.
2. **Structural Fingerprint**: Define a one-line structural signature:
   `concept · scene count · primary hero objects per scene · opening hook · closing payoff`.
   Record this in the style brief and final handoff message to verify differentiation against future deliverables.
3. **Differentiation Across Deliverables**: The concept must differ from prior deliverables, OR at least 3 of 5 fingerprint parameters must be completely distinct. New colors overlaid onto an identical scene sequence remains a template.
4. **Canonical Components Are Not Defaults**: The following elements are permissible only when required by the concept, and **at most TWO** may appear in a single deliverable:
   - Text zooming in and exiting left.
   - 3 parallel feature cards/tiles.
   - Typing input/search bar.
   - Camera push-through between scenes.
   - Light leaks on cut transitions.
   - Centered logo + stacked CTA as the closing scene.
5. **No Universal Sequence**: The formula `Hook → Feature → Feature → Promise → Logo → CTA` is merely one possibility and must never be applied across consecutive projects.
6. **Flexibility Within Anti-PPT Rules**: A scene is not forced to contain "headline + object." Scenes can feature pure UI action, pure typography, or multiple interacting props. What remains mandatory is the Anti-PPT rule: no 3-tier text hierarchies and no fading static sections.
7. **Reference Examples Are Blueprints, Not Scripts**: Example sequences in Concepts 13–19 demonstrate kinetic rhythm, not scripts to clone. When a user requests "Concept X":
   - Extract its underlying visual language and motion dynamics; craft a fresh narrative tailored to the user's brand.
   - The opening hook and closing payoff must differ from the documented examples.
   - Unique moments marked with ✦ must be transformed: borrow the mechanic, but invent brand-native copy and visual forms.
   - The resulting fingerprint must diverge by $\ge 3$ of 5 elements from the documented example.

## Menu of 19 Opener Concepts

| # | Concept | Core Premise | Structural Blueprint | Camera Dynamics & Transitions | Best Suited For |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | One Continuous Shot | Entire video unfolds in a single continuous space without cuts | 1 long sequence, 4–6 visual beats; text anchored onto world surfaces | Camera in continuous motion (dolly, orbit); beats marked by arrival at coordinates | Creative tools, hardware, architectural spaces |
| 2 | Pure Typography | The spoken words are the hero objects; zero mockups | Phrases assemble, fracture, and reorganize; letters form the logo | Rhythm driven by audio track; words enter from 5+ contrasting vectors | Strong taglines, live events, major version releases |
| 3 | Problem $\rightarrow$ Vanished | Environmental chaos resolved by a single product action | 1 scene of escalating chaos $\rightarrow$ decisive product trigger $\rightarrow$ clean order $\rightarrow$ logo | Chaos shakes/accumulates; product action is a wide sweep that clears frame | Productivity tools, utilities, system cleaners |
| 4 | Before / After | Comparative difference viewed side-by-side | Split screen or moving split divider; each slide reveals a feature | The traveling divider acts as the transition | Photo/video editors, filters, optimization tools |
| 5 | Journey Inside the UI | Camera travels within a monumental interface | Buttons serve as platforms; cursor/touch acts as guide; features are landmarks | Volumetric fly-through, UI layer parallax | Applications with distinctive, iconic UI |
| 6 | Product Macro | Extreme close-ups exploring physical details | 4–6 tactile details; minimal text; full product revealed only in finale | Rack focus, slow rotation, light sweeping across material textures | Hardware, packaging, food & beverage, luxury fashion |
| 7 | Object Metaphor | Product portrayed as an evolving physical artifact | A single physical object (key, seed, bridge) morphs throughout, ending as logo | Metamorphic shape morphing carries transitions | Abstract services: cybersecurity, cloud, fintech |
| 8 | Living Number | A single monumental metric tells the story | Metric evolves; each change reveals context (hours saved, bandwidth, scale) | Metric remains anchored; world behind it transforms | Milestones, performance benchmarks, annual reviews |
| 9 | Single Feature Demoed | One signature workflow executed from input to payoff | Input $\rightarrow$ processing $\rightarrow$ satisfying result; other features flash in finale | Camera tracks cursor/touch, cuts into tactile details | Apps with one clear, undeniable competitive edge |
| 10 | Diegetic Q&A | Questions written inside the world; UI provides actions | Questions on billboards, sticky notes, terminal screens $\rightarrow$ product executes | Camera pans from question surface to resolution locus | AI assistants, search engines, customer support |
| 11 | Rhythmic Collage | Rapid fragments synchronized to tempo, returning to motif | 12–20 cuts ($0.3–0.8\text{s}$) + recurring motif every 4 beats | Cut on the beat, geometric match-cuts | Music, youth lifestyle, festivals, community |
| 12 | Logo as Stage | Brand geometry expands to form the physical arena | All action takes place inside logo contours; camera pulls back to reveal logo | Camera dives into negative space and curves of logo | Brands with iconic, highly recognizable geometric logos |
| 13 | Object Relay | A single parcel travels across service stages to the recipient | 4–6 acts (need $\rightarrow$ select $\rightarrow$ gather $\rightarrow$ pack $\rightarrow$ deliver); each act is one action | Transitions CARRIED by the travelling object; backdrops shift | E-commerce, delivery, on-demand logistics, marketplaces |
| 14 | Brand System Showcase | Brand identity is itself the product (logo, typography, palette, stickers) | 8–12 short seamless acts: motif prop $\rightarrow$ logo $\rightarrow$ color field $\rightarrow$ manifesto $\rightarrow$ parade $\rightarrow$ mascot $\rightarrow$ guide $\rightarrow$ loop | Every act emerges from the previous object; solid color fields mark chapters | Rebrands, design agencies, creative communities |
| 15 | Claim $\rightarrow$ How $\rightarrow$ Result | Restrained feature announcement: concise claim, UI in action, blooming result | Repeating cycle: claim ($1–2.5\text{s}$) $\rightarrow$ UI action ($2–6\text{s}$) $\rightarrow$ result ($4–6\text{s}$); closing payoff | Seamless morphs; UI container blooms into result card, then shrinks to point | Generative AI, creative suites, B2B SaaS, pro cameras |
| 16 | Living UI Ecosystem | Product as a connected operational ecosystem | 12–16 short acts: scattered files $\rightarrow$ product icon forms $\rightarrow$ UI assembles $\rightarrow$ workflow $\rightarrow$ integrations $\rightarrow$ payoff | Transitions carried by UI (blooming panels, carousel, flipping icons); max 2 hard cuts | B2B enterprise SaaS, AI workflows, team collaboration |
| 17 | Flat Pop with Photos | Playful consumer lifestyle: photo cutouts, flat brand shapes, color snaps | 15–18 acts ($0.3–3\text{s}$): greeting $\rightarrow$ cutouts + stickers $\rightarrow$ UI triggers background change $\rightarrow$ giant hero words | Background snaps on visible triggers (prop covering lens, UI action, beat cuts) | Consumer fintech, direct-to-consumer apps, youth campaigns |
| 18 | Through Gradient Shapes | Layered glowing brand geometry traversed by camera | 5–8 acts ($2–4\text{s}$): darkness $\rightarrow$ rotating glowing shapes $\rightarrow$ guiding orb $\rightarrow$ tunnel travel $\rightarrow$ portal $\rightarrow$ logo | Seamless; camera travels through negative space of successive layers | Deep tech, cybersecurity, AI infrastructure, music |
| 19 | Product Tour with Claims | Native UI tour pausing periodically on short claims | 9–11 acts ($2–5\text{s}$): title + mini UI $\rightarrow$ dashboard tour $\rightarrow$ lifted card $\rightarrow$ claim $\rightarrow$ split screen $\rightarrow$ analytics | UI-driven transitions (dimming canvas, lifted cards, split screen); 1–2 hard cuts | B2B dashboards, HR suites, business analytics, CRM |

Concepts may be blended (e.g. Concept 9 + Concept 3: demoing one killer feature that cleans up chaotic files), but maintain one primary structural framework.

## Concept 13: Object Relay (Deriving Narrative from Brand)

1. **Service Journey as Acts**: Customer need emerges $\rightarrow$ selection $\rightarrow$ sorting $\rightarrow$ packaging $\rightarrow$ delivery arrival. Trim stages that lack brand distinctiveness.
2. **One Persistent Hero Prop**: An object that evolves form while remaining recognizable: digital item on screen $\rightarrow$ printed order card $\rightarrow$ physical product $\rightarrow$ packaged box $\rightarrow$ parcel unboxed at destination.
3. **Surprising Actors**: Actors do not have to be generic hands holding phones; portray authentic end beneficiaries (e.g. pets shopping for themselves on a veterinary app). Hands, paws, or feet entering the frame are sufficient.
4. **Authentic Props**: Feature real items sold or processed by the brand.
5. **Brand Color as Thread**: The primary brand hue coats the hero prop across every scene, while background environments alternate between light, dark, and white.
6. **Diegetic Branding**: Brand names live inside the environment (labels on boxes, store signage, receipt headers); an explicit end card is optional.

## Concept 14: Brand System Showcase (Layout, Color, Rhythm)

- **Layout**: Centered compositions; hero graphic occupies $25–35\%$ of frame height with generous negative space. Copy is concise ($\le 2$ lines, centered, sentence case). Brand guideline pages appear at massive scale ($70–90\%$ frame width) angled in perspective.
- **Color**: High-key neutral backdrop dominates $\sim 55\%$ of duration; bold brand colors appear in only two key climax scenes ($3\text{s}$ each) as chapter markers.
- **Rhythm**: Zero hard cuts; $25–30\text{s}$ seamless loop. Kinetic typography enters word-by-word locked to musical beats.

## Concept 15: Claim $\rightarrow$ How $\rightarrow$ Result (Restrained Elegance)

- **Layout**: Floating UI components without device bezels, generous rounded corners, wide ambient drop shadows. Zoom into the active control area ($80\%$ frame width). Result cards expand to fill $75–90\%$ of frame height.
- **Color**: Warm off-white canvas ($80\%$), neutral grey UI accents ($15\%$), with color introduced **ONLY** by the product output itself.
- **Rhythm**: Paced transitions ($0.8–1.2\text{s}$ ease in-out). Claims appear over $1–2.5\text{s}$, workflows over $2–6\text{s}$, results over $4–6\text{s}$.

## Concept 16: Living UI Ecosystem (Interactive App & SaaS)

- **Component Assembly**: Construct UI from vector DOM components rather than flat screenshots: headlines, buttons, and active inputs remain crisp, while inactive body text is represented by rounded grey lines.
- **Actor Cursors**: The cursor acts with intention: arrives with ease-out, pauses $0.2\text{s}$, clicks (button scales $0.92 \rightarrow 1.0$), triggering immediate screen reaction. Camera tracks significant clicks.
- **Living Data**: Bar graphs rise sequentially, progress counters roll upward, table rows stagger into place.
- **Transformations**: Panels expand into subsequent workflow stages; file thumbnails fly into drop zones; cards lift off the interface into 3D isometric space.

## Concept 17: Flat Pop with Photos (Youth & Lifestyle)

- **Imagery**: Photographic character cutouts popping up from bottom borders with spring overshoot (`back.out`), overlaid with vector stickers and geometric containers derived from brand logo contours.
- **Background Snapping**: Background colors snap on kinetic triggers: an object crossing the lens, a toggle switch activating, or a product icon scaling to fill the entire viewport.
- **Typography**: Dual scale: small label pills attached to props, contrasted with massive cropped headline words ($30–35\%$ frame height) passing behind characters.

## Object-Driven Transition Menu (Transitions Carried by Props)

- **Next Scene Prop as Wipe**: An incoming device, parcel, or card scales up from the bottom border, completely occluding the previous scene.
- **Leaping Out of Screen**: A selected digital item lifts out of a mockup towards camera, the device folds back, and the item becomes a physical object in the new 3D world.
- **Shape Match-Cut**: An illuminated circle on a dark canvas hard-cuts to a white outline circle on a high-key canvas, evolving into a new object.
- **Pull-Back Context Reveal**: Camera pulls back from a hero object, revealing it is already resting inside its destination room.
- **The Receiving Hand**: A hand or paw enters the frame to retrieve a prop, clearing the canvas for the next act.
- **Leveling Color Field**: A brand color plane sweeps across the frame and **becomes** the background of the subsequent scene; the logo flips color at the boundary line.
- **Symbol Portal**: Camera accelerates directly into the negative space of a brand symbol; its interior luminance expands to form the next scene.
- **Sliding UI Partitions**: Split screen closes inward as the camera zooms into a clicked button.
- **Icon Flips**: A 3D icon rotates $90^\circ$ edge-on; on reverse rotation, its glyph and layout have mutated into the new scene.

## Feature Presentation Menu (Alternatives to the "3 Parallel Tiles" Trap)

- **One Feature Deeply Demoed**: The primary workflow showcased in full, with secondary tools flashing as $0.4\text{s}$ micro-glimpses in the finale.
- **Sequential Word Swap**: A single sentence mutates its final word: "Edit ___" $\rightarrow$ photos $\rightarrow$ videos $\rightarrow$ audio.
- **Metamorphic Object**: An icon representing Feature A physically morphs into Feature B.
- **Shuffled Cards**: Feature cards dealt or shuffled dynamically from a stack.
- **Orbital Hierarchy**: Secondary feature icons orbit the primary hero product before fusing into it.
- **Interactive UI Mockup**: User operates controls; features illuminate directly inside the product interface.
- **Sequential Horizontal Chips**: Multiple rows of capability chips drifting horizontally in alternating directions.
- **Persona Avatar Grid**: Clustered circular avatars popping in, with leader lines drawing out role badges.

## 3-Second Opening Hook Menu

- **In Media Res**: Hero objects are already in motion at second 0.
- **Audio Precedes Visual**: Sound effect or musical beat triggers $0.3\text{s}$ before graphics ignite.
- **Massive Cropped Typography**: Camera pulls back from cropped giant letterforms to reveal the opening statement.
- **Drawing Stroke**: A precision line draws itself, resolving into the brand silhouette.
- **Tactile Macro Texture**: Extreme close-up of material texture pulling back to reveal hardware.
- **Diegetic Typed Input**: Questions typed directly onto an in-world screen or chalkboard.
- **Single Point of Light**: A pinpoint expands into rotating concentric gradient rings.
- **Disorganized Workspace**: Floating windows drift in isometric space before being unified by the product icon.

## Closing Payoff Menu

- **Logo Morphed from Hero Object**: The final hero prop morphs directly into the brand mark.
- **Pull-Back World Reveal**: Camera pulls back to reveal the entire animated environment forms the brand shape.
- **Diegetic Call to Action**: An interactive button inside the UI is pressed, rather than floating static CTA text.
- **Seamless Infinite Loop**: The final frame composition aligns with the opening frame for seamless replay.
- **The Decisive Freeze**: Visual motion halts instantaneously on the final beat as the headline settles.
- **Parcel Reception**: Receiving hands collect the delivered hero parcel; branding lives diegetically on packaging.
- **URL to Brand Swap**: Website URL typed out, backspaced letter-by-letter, and replaced by the clean product name.

## Pre-Delivery Conceptual Checklist

- [ ] Three concept candidates proposed with rationales; one selected based on brand traits.
- [ ] Structural fingerprint explicitly recorded in style brief and handoff message.
- [ ] Concept differs from prior deliverables in at least 3 of 5 fingerprint parameters.
- [ ] Opening hook and closing payoff differ from documented blueprint examples.
- [ ] Palette colors map to brand assets; shapes derived from brand geometry.
- [ ] Maximum of two canonical components utilized.
- [ ] Feature presentation, opening hook, and closing payoff selected intentionally from menus.
- [ ] For Apps/SaaS: at least one living UI demonstration (assembled, operated, producing output).
- [ ] Background moves continuously in every scene; color shifts have visible triggers.
- [ ] Photographic assets sourced and animated with depth and parallax rather than plain Ken Burns pans.
